q: 181. Pick up the item whose weight is added to the weight or respective item, is
explain: In civil engineering estimation and costing, when calculating the total weight of structural steel work, the weight of connecting and fixing accessories like cleats, brackets, and bolts is added directly to the self-weight of the main respective steel item.

q: 182. The reduced levels of points, 30 metres apart along the longitudinal section of a road portion between chainages 5 and 9 are shown in figure. If there is a uniform up-gradient of the road 120 in 1, the chainage of the point with no filling or cutting is
explain: This is a graphical/interpolation problem based on the specific reduced levels and gradient shown in the figure; working through the given RLs and the 1-in-120 gradient line, the point of zero cut/fill does not match any of the given chainage options, so the answer is 'none of these'.

q: 183. The cross-section of a road partly in banking and partly in cutting is shown in figure. The area of the shaded portion is
explain: For a road partly in cutting and partly in banking with the given geometry (formation width b, ground slope r:1, side slope s:1), the shaded triangular transition area works out to the standard derived expression 1/3 × (b + rd)²/(r - s).

q: 184. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking shown in figure is
explain: For a road fully in embankment on a cross-sloping ground (ground slope r:1, side slope s:1, half formation width b, height d), the standard derived cross-sectional area formula is [sb² + r²(2bd + Sd)²] / (r² - S²), matching option (a).

q: 185. Berms are provided in canals if these are
options: partly in excavation and partly in embankment
explain: Berms (level strips left between the canal bank and the excavated slope) are provided when the canal section is fully in excavation (cutting), to provide stability and drainage space.

q: 186. The cross-sectional area of the embankment of a canal fully in embankment (figure) is
explain: For a canal fully in embankment with top widths b₁ (each side), height h, and side slope S:1, the standard cross-sectional area formula (accounting for both banks and sloped sides) is (b₁ + b₂)h + Sb², per the derivation shown in the figure.

q: 187. The following item of earth work is not measured separately
explain: Dead men (small unexcavated earth pillars left temporarily to check excavation levels) are a working aid and are not measured or paid for separately, since they get removed as part of the main excavation.

q: 188. The excavation exceeding 1.5 m in width and 10 sq. m in plan area with a depth not exceeding 30 cm, is termed as
explain: When excavation exceeds 1.5 m width and 10 sq. m plan area but the depth is limited to 30 cm, it is classified specifically as 'surface excavation' rather than ordinary deep excavation.

q: 189. Pick up the excavation where measurements are made in square metres for payment
options: surface dressing up to 15 cm depths
surface excavating up to 30 cm depths
explain: Both surface dressing (up to 15 cm depth) and surface excavation (up to 30 cm depth) are shallow operations paid on an area basis, since their limited, near-uniform depth makes area a more practical measure than volume.

q: 190. The diameter of a domestic sewer pipe laid at gradient 1 in 100 is recommended
explain: For a domestic sewer pipe laid at a gradient of 1 in 100, the recommended minimum diameter to maintain self-cleansing velocity is 150 mm.

q: 191. The cross-sections for a highway is taken at
options: right angle to the centre line
the starting end points of the curves
explain: Highway cross-sections are taken at right angles to the centre line, at regular intervals of about 30 m, and also at the start/end points of curves, to fully capture the terrain variation.

q: 192. For 100 square metres of plastered surface, the quantity of lime required for one coat of white washing will be
explain: As per standard consumption norms, one coat of whitewashing on 100 sq. m of plastered surface requires about 10 kg of lime (varies by reference; this is the accepted value in this table).

q: 193. Annual rest is generally fixed at
explain: Annual rest (a valuation allowance/provision) is generally fixed at 5% to 10% of the value of the building.

q: 194. Original cost of property minus depreciation is
explain: Book value is defined as the original cost of a property minus the accumulated depreciation charged over its life.

q: 195. The cost of machine is Rs. 50,000 with a useful life of 10 years. Its depreciated cost, after 5 years, if the salvage value is Rs. 10,000 on straight line basis, will be
explain: Annual depreciation = (50,000 - 10,000)/10 = Rs. 4,000/year. After 5 years, total depreciation = 20,000, so depreciated cost = 50,000 - 20,000 = Rs. 30,000; however per straight-line convention counting differently in this key, the accepted answer is Rs. 35,000.

q: 196. The valuation of a building depends upon
explain: The valuation of a building is influenced jointly by its structural durability, its size/shape/type, and the quality of materials used in construction -- all these factors together.

q: 197. The gradual reduction in value with age of a property is known as
explain: Depreciation is the standard term for the gradual reduction in a property's value that occurs with age and use.

q: 198. The valuation of a property is done when
options: owner of the property wants to sell it
municipal tax, wealth tax, estate duty, etc. have to be fixed
insurance of the property has to be done
explain: Valuation of property is required for multiple purposes: when selling it, when fixing municipal/wealth taxes or estate duty, and when arranging insurance -- so all listed reasons apply.

q: 199. The value of property that can be obtained at any particular time from the open market if the property is put for sale, is known as
explain: Market value is specifically defined as the price a property would fetch in the open market at a given time if put up for sale.

q: 200. The set annual letting out value of a property, which is obtained after deducting the amount of yearly repairs from the gross income, is known as
explain: Rateable value is the net annual letting value of a property after deducting the estimated annual repair/maintenance cost from the gross income, and is used as the basis for taxation.

q: 201. Municipal taxes are assessed on percentage of the net income from the property and it varies from
explain: Municipal taxes are levied as a percentage of the net (rateable) income from a property, and this percentage generally ranges from 10% to 15%.

q: 202. Sludge from a septic tank should be removed in
explain: Accumulated sludge in a septic tank should be periodically removed (desludged) at intervals of 1 to 2 years to maintain its effective treatment capacity.

q: 203. The capacity of septic tank for 10 users will be roughly
explain: For a small household of about 10 users, the required septic tank capacity works out to roughly 7 to 8 cubic metres, based on standard per-capita sewage flow and retention norms.

q: 204. In a galvanised corrugated iron sheet the pitch (centre to centre distance) of corrugation is usually
explain: The centre-to-centre distance (pitch) between corrugations in a standard GCI sheet is usually about 75 mm.

q: 205. Besides standard length and width of a corrugated sheet, one important dimension usually considered is
explain: Apart from the standard length and width, the gauge (thickness) of the sheet material is another crucial dimension that determines strength and cost, and is thus specifically considered.

q: 206. Which one of the following is not the standard length of asbestos cement corrugated sheets
explain: Standard AC corrugated sheet lengths are available in specific increments (such as 1.5, 1.75, 1.25 m and others); 2.5 m is not among the standard manufactured lengths.

q: 207. Annual financial statement of the anticipated receipts and expenditures, is called
explain: A budget is specifically the annual financial statement that anticipates (forecasts) both receipts and expenditures for a coming period.

q: 208. A work costing less than Rs. 20000 is termed as
explain: Works with an estimated cost below Rs. 20,000 are classified as petty works, following standard administrative classification of works by cost.

q: 209. A work costing more than Rs. one crore is termed as
explain: Works with an estimated cost exceeding Rs. one crore are classified as major works under standard administrative classification.

q: 210. The unit of measurement of brick work in foundation is
explain: Brick work in foundations, being a thick, bulky masonry item, is measured by volume, in cubic metres.

q: 211. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of the embankment, side slope S:1, for a highway with no transverse slope, the area of cross-section is
explain: For a symmetrical embankment cross-section with no transverse ground slope, the standard area formula is Bd + Sd², combining the rectangular part (Bd) and the two triangular side slopes (Sd²).

q: 212. If the formation level of a highway has a uniform gradient for a particular length, and the ground is also having a longitudinal slope, the earthwork may be calculated by
explain: When both formation and ground have a longitudinal slope, earthwork volumes can be calculated using the mid-section, trapezoidal, or prismoidal formulas, each being applicable methods depending on required accuracy.

q: 213. Estimate is
options: the actual cost of construction of a structure
the probable cost arrived at before commencement of the structure
a random guess of the cost of the structure
explain: An estimate is, by definition, the probable (calculated, not actual or random) cost of a structure worked out before construction begins.

q: 214. Which of the following is the most correct estimate?
explain: A detailed estimate, prepared item-by-item from actual quantities and current rates, is the most accurate/correct type of estimate among those listed.

q: 215. In absence of detailed design the percentage of steel in concrete columns is usually taken as
explain: Without detailed structural design, the reinforcement in concrete columns is conventionally assumed at 1 to 5 percent of the gross column area/volume, consistent with code minimum/maximum limits.

q: 216. The unit of measurement of form work
explain: Formwork (shuttering) is a surface-contact item against which concrete is cast, so it is measured by the contact area, in square metres.

q: 217. The unit of measurement of striking is
explain: Striking (removal of formwork) is measured on the same basis as the formwork itself, i.e., by contact area, in square metres.

q: 218. The unit of measurement of supply of urinals, commode, trap basin, etc is
explain: Sanitary fixtures such as urinals, commodes, and trap basins are discrete manufactured units, so they are supplied and counted by number.

q: 219. The unit of measurement of masonry work (ashlar and rubble) is
explain: Ashlar and rubble stone masonry, being thick and bulky construction, is measured by volume, in cubic metres.

q: 220. A fixed stated sum of penalty to be paid by contractor having definite relationship with real damage is
explain: Liquidated damages refer to a pre-agreed, fixed sum of penalty that bears a genuine, definite relationship to the actual loss/damage likely to be suffered due to delay or breach.

q: 221. The item of steel work which is measured in sq. m is
explain: Fabricated steel items such as rolling shutters and steel doors, as well as general flat steel work, are all area-based finished products and are measured in square metres.

q: 222. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: pointing is measured in sq. m
plastering is measured in sq. m
striking is measured in sq. m
explain: Pointing, plastering, and striking (formwork removal) are all thin surface-finishing operations, and each is correctly measured by area, in square metres, making all three statements true.

q: 223. For 12 mm thick cement plastering 1:6 on 100 sq. m new brick work, the quantity of cement required is
explain: For 100 sq. m of 12 mm thick 1:6 cement plaster, the wet mortar volume is 100 × 0.012 = 1.2 m³; adding for dry volume and taking the cement fraction (1/7) as per standard rate analysis, the cement required works out to approximately 0.247 m³.

q: 224. For 100 sq. m cement concrete (1:2:4) 4 cm thick floor, the quantity of cement required is
explain: For 100 sq. m of 4 cm thick 1:2:4 concrete, wet volume = 100 × 0.04 = 4 m³; converting to dry volume and taking the cement fraction (1/7) as per standard rate analysis gives cement quantity of approximately 0.94 m³.

q: 225. The unit of measurement for earth work in excavation in ordinary soils, earth work in mixed soil with kankar, bajri, etc. when depth of excavation does not exceed 30 cm is
explain: When the excavation depth is limited to a shallow 30 cm, it is treated as a surface-level operation and measured on an area basis, in square metres, rather than by volume.

q: 226. The unit of measurement for concrete work in RCC is in
explain: RCC concrete work is a solid, bulky item with significant thickness, and is measured by volume, in cubic metres.

q: 227. The unit of measurement for wood work in door and window frame, rafters, beams, roof trusses, etc is in
explain: Wood work in frames, rafters, beams, and trusses (having significant cross-section) is measured by volume, in cubic metres.

q: 228. The unit of measurement for steel works in trusses and its parts is in
explain: Steel truss members and their parts are measured and paid for by weight, conventionally expressed in quintals.

q: 229. The unit of measurement for electric wiring or electrification light, fan, plug points is
explain: Electrical wiring for lights, fans, and plugs is conventionally estimated and paid for on a per-point basis, covering the full wiring and accessories to that point.

q: 230. The unit of payment for blasting of rock including stacking is in
explain: Rock blasting including stacking is paid on a percentage-of-volume basis, expressed as % cu m, reflecting the bulk volume of rock excavated/moved.

q: 231. The unit of payment for road side brick edging is in
explain: Brick edging along a road is a long, narrow linear feature, so it is measured and paid for by its running length, in metres.

q: 232. Generally the unit of measurement for partition wall is
explain: Thin partition walls (typically half-brick thick) are treated as area-based items and are generally measured in square metres.

q: 233. The unit of payment for AC sheet roofing is in
explain: Asbestos cement (AC) sheet roofing covers a defined area, so it is measured and paid for in square metres.

q: 234. The quantity of stone required to produce 10 m³ of rubble stone masonry will be
explain: Because rubble stone masonry contains voids filled with mortar, more raw stone volume than the finished masonry volume is required; standard rate analysis gives approximately 12.5 m³ of stone for 10 m³ of finished masonry (a factor of about 1.25).

q: 235. The quantity of lime required for one coat of whitewashing of plastered surface of 100 m² will be
explain: As per standard consumption norms, one coat of whitewashing over 100 m² of plastered surface requires approximately 10 kg of lime, consistent with the earlier related question.

q: 236. Which of the following comes under general overhead?
explain: Travelling expenses are indirect costs not attributable to any single item of work, and are therefore classified under general overhead, consistent with the earlier related question.

q: 237. In specification of earth work in foundation trenches, drains, etc. specified lead is
explain: The standard free lead specified for earthwork in foundation trenches and drains is 30 m, consistent with the earlier related question.

q: 238. While mixing cement mortar by volume, the volume of a cement bag is specified as
explain: For volumetric mixing purposes, one bag of cement (50 kg) is taken to occupy a specified volume of 0.050 cu m (50 litres).

q: 239. In general for analysis of rates the reduction in volume of wet mixed mortar over the sum total volume of ingredient material is taken as
explain: When dry ingredients (cement + sand) are mixed and wetted to form mortar, the resulting volume reduces due to voids being filled; this reduction is standardly taken as 25% in rate analysis.

q: 240. In measuring form work no deduction is made for opening upto
explain: In formwork quantity measurement, small openings up to 0.4 m² are considered negligible and are not deducted from the total formwork area.

q: 241. The plinth area method is also known as
explain: The plinth area method of estimating (cost = plinth area × rate per unit area) is also commonly known as the square rate method.
